items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: Yeah, he took a couple of lessons. He didn't stay, but he took enough to learn to play pretty good.

ctx.x: But still, it'd be better than almost anybody can do now. Oh, yeah. I've never heard, I'm sure. Yeah, these fellas are playing now. I don't know. I'm not knocking, I'm not knocking like that. But, I don't know, they don't seem to get the right bass on, you know, on trombone. It seem like they're off some way. It seem like they're way back. And sometimes I pick up, sometime on the radio, hear some fellas playing, and he's alright, but there's a few of them, see? Yeah. And the majority, they look like as many bands…
There's one other New Orleans tromboneist here, Albert Wynn. Do you know that?
Yeah, he took a couple of lessons. He didn't stay, but he took enough to learn to play pretty good. He plays pretty good.
